title: Using Amigo with Google Meet | Amigo — AI Career Companion & Interview Copilot
description: Connect Amigo to Google Meet interviews. Setup, audio capture, and tips for a real-time AI copilot that stays out of Meet's screen share.
html:
Google Meet is a common choice for interviews at tech companies and startups. Because Meet runs entirely in a browser tab, Amigo's desktop overlay is never captured by Meet's screen share, and audio works out of the box on both macOS and Windows.

Setup

  1. Install the Amigo desktop app; see the Installation guide.
  2. On macOS, grant Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions when prompted on first launch.
  3. Open Amigo and run the Audio Check to verify system audio is captured.
  4. Open Google Meet in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge; any Chromium-based browser works best.
  5. Join your meeting. Amigo will begin listening automatically.

Chrome is recommended for Google Meet. It uses the least CPU among supported browsers, leaving more resources for Amigo's transcription process.

Screen Sharing

Google Meet offers three share modes. All three are safe to use with Amigo:

  • Your entire screen: Amigo is excluded at the OS level; the interviewer will not see the overlay.
  • A window: Only the selected window is shared. Amigo is never in scope.
  • A Chrome tab: Tab sharing is isolated to that browser tab. Amigo is not captured.

Browser Audio Permissions

Google Meet requires microphone access from the browser. This is separate from Amigo's system audio capture. You do not need to give Amigo access to your browser microphone; Amigo reads the audio at the OS level, independently.

  • Allow microphone access to Meet in the browser prompt (this is for your call audio only).
  • Amigo captures system audio independently; no browser extension is required.
  • If Meet asks you to "allow screen sharing audio", you can skip this; Amigo handles audio separately.

Known Issues

  • macOS: audio not captured in Incognito mode: Chrome Incognito tabs may not route audio through the system audio device Amigo listens to. Use a regular Chrome window for Meet.
  • Firefox on Windows: slight latency increase: Firefox routes audio differently from Chromium on Windows, which can add ~200 ms to transcription. Switch to Chrome if latency is noticeable.
  • Meet noise cancellation: Google Meet's built-in noise suppression is applied before audio reaches Amigo. If transcription quality is poor, disable noise suppression in Meet Settings → Audio.

No browser extension is needed. Amigo is a native desktop application and captures system audio directly, so there is nothing to install in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge.
